summary: Jitsuzo Kuwabara was a scholar in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (c. 1892–1896) and held posts at Third Higher School, Tokyo Higher Normal School, and Kyoto Imperial University.
Jiun Kubota is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied under traditional teacher Kyozo Yamada and succeeded Koun Yamada.

Jivnesh Sandhan works in computational linguistics and Indology. He completed a PhD at IIT Kanpur under Laxmidhar Behera and held posts at UC Berkeley, Kyoto University as a postdoc, IIT Kanpur, and IIT Dharwad (attested 2025).

Jiyu Ren was a scholar of religion, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Lin He, he held faculty posts there, directed the CASS Institute of World Religions, and was honorary director of the National Library.

Jiyu-Kennett worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Trinity Laban, Durham, and Soji-ji under Seck Kim Seng, Keidō Chisan Kōho, and Suigan Yogo. She served as head priest at Unpukuji and founded and served as abbess of Shasta Abbey.
Joachim Friedrich Sprockhoff is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Friedrich Otto Schrader and Helmuth von Glasenapp.

Joachim Gentz works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He served as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and as Reader (attested 2013) and Professor (attested 2026) in Chinese Studies at the University of Edinburgh.

Joachim Heidrich was an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin under Walter Ruben. He held posts at the Zentralinstitut für Geschichte (1981–1989) and the Leibniz-Zentrum Moderner Orient (c. 1992–1995).

Joachim Menant was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Caen Normandy, held a post at the University of Paris, and became a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres in 1888.
Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Vienna by 1994, studying under Gerhard Oberhammer.

Joachim Wach was a scholar of religion and philosophy. Educated at multiple universities including Leipzig and Heidelberg, he held academic positions at the University of Leipzig, Brown University, and the University of Chicago.

Joan Jiko Halifax is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD from Union Institute & University and trained under Seungsahn Haengwon and Bernie Glassman, holding posts at Columbia, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and Harvard, among others.

Joan Mascaró was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Cambridge from circa 1923 to 1926 and served as Professor of English at the University of Barcelona in 1933.

Joanna Bialek is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who completed her PhD at the University of Marburg in 2016. She held postdoctoral posts at Humboldt University of Berlin, Trinity College Dublin, and the University of Munich.
Joanna Cook is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She studied under advisor James Laidlaw and held a post at Christ's College, Cambridge.

Joanna Gottfried Williams was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University, and served on the faculty at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1969 to 2004.

Joanna Grela is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at INALCO, Jagiellonian University, and SWPS University. She held a faculty post as professor at Jagiellonian University in 2006.
Joanna Macy was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She completed her studies at Wellesley College (c. 1946–1950) and Syracuse University (c. 1973–1978).

Joanne Punzo Waghorne is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago. She held academic posts at UMass Boston, Bowdoin College, UNC Chapel Hill, and Syracuse University.

Joannes van der Vliet was an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned his PhD at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He held posts at the University of Amsterdam and Utrecht University.
